properties.name: A writing --call keeps the committed export current before it exits (step 2 of the --call door plan)
properties.rationale: THE CAUSE, confirmed on main c4e1cbd before any change (measure script, not inferred): in a folder whose .mcp.json names --export-to ./docs/design/proj.json, --call add_requirement exited 0, stderr empty, the export's sha256 unchanged, req absent from it, compare_designs identical:false; --export-to with --call was refused by the item-1 gate. call_one_tool installs no write-through, and start_auto_export runs only in the serving branches. Starting it would not have helped: AutoExport is a spawned task waiting 2 s for quiet and call_over_pipe tears the server down when the reply arrives (fact:root-cause-call-accepts-export-to-and-never-reads-it-2026-10-02). THE CLASS: a guarantee built as a background task of a long-lived server does not hold for a process that serves one call. THE FIX REUSES THE PATH, IT DOES NOT COPY IT: ReflowService::keep_export_current_at_exit installs the same AutoExport without spawning; export_now pokes and flushes it (the flush a draining server already uses). So the door obeys every write-through rule by construction. WHEN: a write by its served annotation that succeeded (exit 0), per the requirement; the unit (#655) discards a refused or errored call, so those owe nothing. WHERE: the path is what a long-lived server for THIS store would be started with — the --export-to in the project's MCP config whose --graph-path is this store — never history or a naming convention (the 2026-09-12 explicit-path ruling recorded in auto_export.rs). LEFT OUT, deliberately: --import (the mode) loads the record INTO the store, so writing the store back over it would turn a restore into an edit of the committed file; --call import_graph is a served write and is covered. Claude Code's user-scope ~/.claude.json entries are not read (a project file only). COST AND --no-export: On reflow2's own design (6,478 nodes, 41,875 edges, a 28 MB export; release build, medians of five) a write took 1.65 s alone and 6.0 s with its export; export_graph took 3.1 s to a new path and 5.1 s onto the committed path; peak 413 MB. So a --no-export flag was added for scripted bulk writes (honoured by --call only, refused with --export-to); it says the export is behind. The default keeps it current.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: A --call that writes and succeeds now writes the project's design export before the process exits, by the server's own write-through (AutoExport) installed with no background task and run synchronously: the replaced-binary check, the hand-edit guard, lineage from the committed record, never accept_divergence. The file is --export-to (now HONOURED with --call; item 1's table row changed), else the --export-to the project's MCP configuration names for this store; else none, and one stderr line says so. Reads, refused writes and tool errors write no export. One stderr line says where it was written; exit 3 when the write landed and the export could not be written. Configurations naming different files are refused before anything opens.
